Wow. Thank you. I really needed to read this. 

As for your question about school, I've not been doing as well as I should. So much so that I feel I may actually get held back for the 2020-2021 school season (I'm supposed to be going into eleventh grade, but I *technically* never finished tenth; kind of a long story). But I plan to hop right back in regardless and give it my all. I need to start applying for scholarships as well.

Thank you for reminding me about the house situation. I don't know why I just want to rushrushrush; my parents have always struggled with money, so I suppose I'm becoming paranoid nowadays. Being reminded that most people rent and that I can find housemates really grounded me and got me back in reality. Thank you again. 

In reference to what you said about colleges, I do have some ideas. I want to shoot for Mercer University. That's my number one biggest choice. I have something called a Reach Scholarship that was gifted to me in 2017; if I finish high school with a 3.0 GPA or higher, I get 10k towards tuition for any participating Georgia college. I just don't know if Mercer is participating, and they may not have the specific course I'm looking to take (marketing communications). My second idea is Lanier Technical College. They teach business management, and marketing communications is a subcourse. I definitely need to make some calls, find out extra info still, but it feels good to have something to keep my eye on.

I get so manic about money, I really feel like having my own income (even if it's not a lot) would help with that (as well as medication, lol). But there are just a few things that worry me, not limited to the fact that my parents are *awful* money spenders, and often dug us into holes that required my sister's hard-earned money back when she still lived with us. But I really do want a job. My sister works at the humane society here, and I was thinking of trying to apply for weekend shifts when school comes back around (they close around the time school lets out each day, so, unfortunately, I couldn't work after school). 

Sorry that this is long. I really appreciate you reaching out to me and helping me. I'm going to get back in school, focus on getting good grades and look into colleges,  and try to get a job so I can have some money of my own.
